reading.title: NIL and Void: A Legal Analysis of College Athletes' Broadcast Rights of Publicity as Created by the House Settlement
reading.source: Journal of College and University Law (NACUA), April 17, 2026
reading.text:
On June 6, 2025, Judge Claudia Wilken of the Northern District of California granted final approval of the $2.576–$2.8 billion class action settlement in In re: College Athlete NIL Litigation, commonly known as the House Settlement. The plaintiffs — led by former Arizona State swimmer Grant House and Oregon basketball player Sedona Prince — challenged NCAA and athletics conference rules that restricted or entirely prohibited college athlete compensation for the use of their name, image, or likeness (NIL), including NIL as captured and monetized in television and streaming broadcasts.

The central legal argument advanced by a new academic analysis is that the House Settlement created a novel category of rights labeled "Broadcast NIL" — or BNIL — representing compensation tied specifically to athlete appearances in televised athletic events. However, the authors contend that the doctrinal foundation for recognizing BNIL as a cognizable right of publicity is, in their words, "thin at best." Tracing precedent through O'Bannon v. NCAA, Marshall v. ESPN, and NCAA v. Alston, the analysis emphasizes that courts have consistently held that individual athletes do not possess common-law rights of publicity in broadcast events, because it is the producer — not the athlete-participant — whose interests copyright and broadcast law have traditionally protected.

The settlement further mandates that all third-party NIL deals valued at $600 or more must be reported and reviewed through the NIL Go clearinghouse, operated by Deloitte and the College Sports Commission (CSC). Critically, such arrangements must reflect genuine fair market value and a valid business purpose, rather than functioning as disguised pay-for-play inducements. School revenue-sharing payments are capped at $20.5 million annually per institution for the 2025–26 academic year.

The authors argue that because BNIL lacks firm grounding under existing publicity-rights doctrine, the settlement framework will likely face additional judicial scrutiny and is ultimately unsustainable absent new federal legislation. Reinforcing this view, a follow-on lawsuit — Jenkins v. NCAA, filed April 5, 2025 in the Southern District of New York — is already seeking damages for broadcast NIL use by the NCAA and Power Five conferences, signaling that litigation pressure continues to mount even following the House Settlement's final approval.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 集体诉讼和解协议：代表一类具有共同法律主张的原告群体与被告达成的终结诉讼的协议，须经法院审查批准方可生效。
vocabulary.example: The $2.576–$2.8 billion class action settlement in In re: College Athlete NIL Litigation was granted final approval by Judge Wilken in June 2025.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 姓名、肖像或形象权（NIL）：个人对其身份标识商业性使用所享有的人格财产权，是美国公开权（right of publicity）的核心要素。
vocabulary.example: The NCAA's longstanding prohibition on compensation for the use of an athlete's name, image, or likeness was a central grievance in the House Settlement litigation.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 公开权：个人控制其姓名、肖像或形象被商业利用的财产性权利，通常由州普通法或制定法确立，与隐私权性质不同。
vocabulary.example: The academic authors argued that recognizing BNIL as a cognizable right of publicity lacks firm grounding in existing broadcast law doctrine.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 广播NIL（BNIL）：House和解协议所创设的一种新型权利类别，指运动员出现于电视转播赛事中所对应的姓名肖像形象补偿权，其法律基础尚存争议。
vocabulary.example: Critics contend that Broadcast NIL, as defined by the House Settlement, has no established precedent under American publicity-rights doctrine.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 以运动表现换取报酬的诱导行为：指以招募或保留运动员为目的，以NIL合同形式掩盖的实质性运动薪酬支付，被监管框架明确禁止。
vocabulary.example: Under the House Settlement framework, third-party NIL arrangements must reflect genuine fair market value rather than functioning as disguised pay-for-play inducements.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 收益分成：指院校将部分媒体、赛事或赞助收益按约定比例直接分配给运动员的机制，House和解协议将其上限设定为每校每学年2050万美元。
vocabulary.example: School revenue-sharing payments are capped at $20.5 million annually per institution for the 2025–26 academic year under the settlement's terms.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 信息审查交换所：此处指由德勤及大学体育委员会运营的NIL Go系统，负责接收、审查并核实NIL合同的公平市场价值与商业目的合规性。
vocabulary.example: All third-party NIL deals valued at $600 or more must be reported and reviewed through the NIL Go clearinghouse operated by Deloitte and the College Sports Commission.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 公平市场价值：在自愿买卖双方充分知情且无强迫情形下，某项资产或服务在公开市场应有的合理价格，NIL监管体系以此判断合同是否构成变相招募违规。
vocabulary.example: The settlement requires that NIL arrangements must reflect genuine fair market value rather than serving as a recruitment subsidy.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 业余体育原则：NCAA长期坚持的规则体系，禁止大学运动员获取运动竞技报酬以维持其"业余"身份，该原则已在多起联邦诉讼中受到严重冲击。
vocabulary.example: The settlement attempts to thread the needle of compensating athletes while formally preserving the amateurism model that courts have increasingly called into question.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 司法审查：法院对协议、规则或行政行为进行实质性审查评估的程序，用于判断其是否符合法律标准，在反垄断与集体诉讼和解语境中尤为关键。
vocabulary.example: Because BNIL lacks firm grounding under existing publicity-rights doctrine, the settlement framework will likely face additional judicial scrutiny in coming years.

sentence_patterns.pattern: [Court] granted final approval of [settlement], holding that [legal basis or finding].
sentence_patterns.example: Judge Claudia Wilken of the Northern District of California granted final approval of the $2.576–$2.8 billion class action settlement, holding that the framework adequately addressed college athletes' claims for NIL compensation.
sentence_patterns.translation_cn: 北加州联邦地区法院法官克劳迪娅·威尔肯批准了总额达25.76至28亿美元的集体诉讼和解协议，认定该框架充分回应了大学运动员的NIL补偿诉求。

sentence_patterns.pattern: Because [doctrine/right] lacks firm grounding under existing [legal framework], [settlement/statute] will likely face additional [legal challenge].
sentence_patterns.example: Because Broadcast NIL lacks firm grounding under existing publicity-rights doctrine, the settlement framework will likely face additional judicial scrutiny absent new federal legislation.
sentence_patterns.translation_cn: 由于广播NIL在现行公开权法律框架下缺乏坚实的法律依据，该和解框架在缺乏新联邦立法的情况下，极有可能面临进一步的司法审查。

sentence_patterns.pattern: [Arrangement] must reflect genuine [standard], rather than functioning as disguised [prohibited conduct].
sentence_patterns.example: Third-party NIL arrangements must reflect genuine fair market value and a valid business purpose, rather than functioning as disguised pay-for-play inducements.
sentence_patterns.translation_cn: 第三方NIL安排必须体现真实的公平市场价值和正当商业目的，而不得作为变相的以运动表现换取报酬的诱导手段。

summary_cn: 2025年6月，加州联邦地区法院正式批准总额约28亿美元的House和解协议，终结NCAA NIL集体诉讼。协议创设"广播NIL"（BNIL）这一新型权利类别，并规定院校年度收益分成上限为2050万美元，同时要求600美元以上NIL合同须经NIL Go清算所审核。但学界批评认为BNIL缺乏既有法律依据，后续诉讼（Jenkins v. NCAA）已经提起，联邦立法压力持续加大。
legal_analysis:
① 核心法律问题：House和解协议在未经国会立法明确授权的情况下，试图通过诉讼和解方式创设"广播NIL"这一全新的公开权类别，其法律正当性存在根本性疑问。

② 美国法律框架分析：美国公开权（right of publicity）传统上属于州法保护的个人人格财产权，但在体育广播语境下，法院（包括O'Bannon v. NCAA及Marshall v. ESPN等案）一贯认为广播权归属于赛事制作者而非运动员参与者，版权法亦持相同立场。NCAA v. Alston（2021年）虽动摇了业余体育原则的反垄断豁免基础，但并未正面确认运动员享有BNIL。和解框架通过NIL Go清算所强制合规审查，并以"公平市场价值"标准防止变相薪酬，体现了反垄断合规与NCAA监管改革的双重压力。

③ 对中国娱乐法律师的实践启示：中国律师在处理跨国体育赛事转播授权、运动员肖像权商业化以及MCN/经纪合同时，应关注：其一，"广播NIL"概念对运动员肖像权主体地位的重构可能影响中美联合赛事授权谈判结构；其二，美国NIL清算所审查机制可为中国赛事组织者设计运动员商业权益合规管理体系提供制度参考；其三，Jenkins v. NCAA等后续诉讼的走向将直接影响跨境体育媒体版权的风险评估。
cn_us_comparison: 在美国，公开权（right of publicity）由各州制定法或普通法保护，属个人对其姓名、肖像商业利用的财产性权利，House和解协议在此基础上进一步延伸至体育广播场景。相比之下，中国对运动员姓名、肖像权的保护主要依据《民法典》第一千零一十八条至一千零二十三条（肖像权）及第一千一百二十四条（姓名权），以人格权为核心框架，不具备美国公开权的独立财产权性质。在体育广播转播权方面，中国主要适用《著作权法》对视听作品的保护，转播权归属赛事组织者或制作者，运动员个人通常不享有独立的广播NIL请求权，与美国BNIL争议所呈现的权利主体扩张趋势存在显著差异。此外，中国尚无类似NIL Go清算所的专门NIL合规审查机制，运动员商业代言主要通过经纪合同及体育总局相关规范性文件加以规范，立法层面的系统性框架仍有待建立。
discussion_prompt: Given that courts have consistently held that broadcast rights vest in the producer rather than the athlete-participant, should the legal recognition of Broadcast NIL require affirmative federal legislation — and if so, which model, the SCORE Act or the SAFE Act, better addresses the doctrinal gap exposed by the House Settlement?

writing_exercise.prompt: Imagine you are a legal analyst writing a brief memo. In 2-3 sentences, explain why the Broadcast NIL framework created by the House Settlement may face ongoing judicial scrutiny, using precise legal terminology from the reading.
writing_exercise.model_answer: Because Broadcast NIL lacks firm grounding under existing publicity-rights doctrine — as affirmed in O'Bannon v. NCAA and Marshall v. ESPN — the settlement framework will likely face additional judicial scrutiny unless Congress enacts legislation affirmatively recognizing athletes' claims. The House Settlement attempts to thread the needle between compensating athletes and preserving the amateurism model, yet without a statutory foundation for BNIL, courts may reject the premise that athlete appearances in broadcast events constitute a cognizable right of publicity. Reinforcing this concern, Jenkins v. NCAA, filed in the Southern District of New York, signals that litigation pressure will continue to mount even following the settlement's final approval.

youtube_rec.summary_cn: 本视频系统解析House和解协议的核心条款，包括广播NIL的法律争议、NIL Go清算所的合规审查机制、收益分成上限规则，以及Jenkins v. NCAA后续诉讼对整个大学体育法律框架的潜在冲击，适合希望深入理解美国NIL立法走向的法律从业者。

extended_reading.description_cn: Snell & Wilmer律所比较分析SCORE法案与SAFE法案在反垄断安全港、运动员雇佣分类及广播权立法授权方面的核心分歧。
